query: The Breakfast Engine Mir slides a breakfast tray across to you. "Practice! Make it do breakfast. Toast, butter, tea. It's the hardest machine there is, probably." Half the refectory has already turned to watch. Build the breakfast engine Your engine butters four slices, pours one cup and singes your eyebrow before it falls apart in a shower of crumbs. The refectory applauds. Mir writes something down, beaming. Build it with Mir, slowly You build it together, Mir explaining every joint. It makes one perfect slice of toast and then retires. Mir says it's the best machine of the year, probably.

It Probably Works
Mir sweeps a bench clear with one arm. "Watch!" A kettle, a mantel clock and a spoon jump together into a whirring thing that pours tea, mostly into the cup. "No plans, no drawings, just ask the bits what they want to be! It's my own. It probably won't explode.

results.title: The Artificers' Fair
results.excerpt:
The Artificers' Fair
The Artificers' Fair. Mir's entry is under a sheet and occasionally growls. "I need an assistant to stand next to it and look confident," they say. "And possibly run."
Watch from a safe distance
The machine turns out to be a mechanical bear that bakes bread.

results.title: Blueprints
results.excerpt:
Blueprints
Mir has drawn a blueprint for something for you. {~"A lamp that turns itself off when you fall asleep reading," they say. "Probably."|"A pocket that's bigger inside," they say. "In theory. In practice, it eats keys."} They don't say why they keep making things for you.
